# system-configs

NixOS configuration for two hosts, structured with the dendritic flake-parts
pattern.

| Host | Hardware | Role |
|------|----------|------|
| `serenity` | Framework Desktop (AMD AI Max+ 395) | Plasma 6 desktop, gaming, local LLM serving |
| `nostromo` | Framework 13 (AMD 7040) | niri + Noctalia laptop, home-manager |

Rebuild a host from a checkout of this repo:

```
sudo nixos-rebuild switch --flake <path-to-this-repo>#<hostname>
```

## How it works

**`flake.nix` is generated.** Do not edit it. Each module declares the flake
inputs it needs via `flake-file.inputs.<name>` next to where the input is
used; `nix run .#write-flake` collects the declarations and rewrites
`flake.nix`. The `outputs` expression it writes hands the entire `modules/`
tree to flake-parts:

```nix
inputs: inputs.flake-parts.lib.mkFlake { inherit inputs; } (inputs.import-tree ./modules)
```

**Every `*.nix` file under `modules/` is a flake-parts module.** import-tree
imports them all, recursively — there are no import lists to maintain. Files
whose path contains a `_`-prefixed component and non-Nix files (`.kbd`,
`.md`, …) are ignored, so assets and notes can sit next to the modules that
use them.

**Features are deferred modules.** A file contributes configuration by
merging into a named module under `flake.modules.<class>.<name>`, where
class is `nixos` or `homeManager`. Many files can define the same name; the
module system merges them. Nothing happens until some host imports the name
— importing a module is what enables it.

**Hosts are names.** Every file in `modules/hosts/serenity/` merges into
`flake.modules.nixos.serenity`. The `host.nix` file there adds host identity
(hostname, stateVersion), imports the shared aspects
(`inputs.self.modules.nixos.pc`, `.shashin`, …), and turns the merged module
into the flake output:

```nix
flake.nixosConfigurations.serenity = inputs.nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
  system = "x86_64-linux";
  modules = [ inputs.self.modules.nixos.serenity ];
};
```

**No specialArgs.** A file that needs a flake input takes `inputs` as a
top-level flake-parts module argument and closes over it inside the deferred
module body:

```nix
{ inputs, ... }:
{
  flake.modules.nixos.pc = { pkgs, ... }: {
    environment.systemPackages = [
      inputs.claude-code-statusline.packages.${pkgs.system}.default
    ];
  };
}
```

## Layout

```
flake.nix                  generated by flake-file — never edit by hand
modules/
  flake/dendritic.nix      core wiring: flake-parts modules option, flake-file, systems
  flake/nixpkgs.nix        the nixpkgs input declaration
  pc/                      shared baseline, one feature per file → flake.modules.nixos.pc
                           (boot, disko, impermanence, amd-graphics, tpm, networking,
                            locale, audio, zram, mullvad, security, nix-settings,
                            openldap-overlay, fontconfig, xdg-portal, packages,
                            services, bluetooth, programs)
  users/shashin/
    user.nix               the OS account → flake.modules.nixos.shashin
    home-manager.nix       HM wiring for a host → flake.modules.nixos.home-shashin
    home/                  HM config → flake.modules.homeManager.shashin
    firefox.nix            UNWIRED: flake.modules.homeManager.firefox (needs a nur input)
    htop.nix               UNWIRED: flake.modules.homeManager.htop
  hosts/serenity/          → flake.modules.nixos.serenity + output wiring in host.nix
  hosts/nostromo/          → flake.modules.nixos.nostromo + output wiring in host.nix
    power-profile.nix      UNWIRED: flake.modules.nixos.power-profile
tools/                     verify-parity.sh / drv-equiv.sh — evaluation comparison harness
skills/dendritic-module/   agent skill for extending this config
dotfiles/                  GNU stow tree, applied manually — never read by Nix
INSTALL.md                 from-blank-machine install runbook
```

Unwired modules are defined but imported by nothing; they evaluate to
nothing and cost nothing until a host or user imports them.

## Do

- **Add a shared feature**: create one file under `modules/pc/` that merges
  into `flake.modules.nixos.pc`. Both hosts get it — no other edits.
- **Add a host-specific feature**: create a file under
  `modules/hosts/<host>/` merging into `flake.modules.nixos.<host>`.
- **Add home-manager config**: create a file under
  `modules/users/shashin/home/` merging into
  `flake.modules.homeManager.shashin`.
- **Add a flake input**: declare `flake-file.inputs.<name>` in the module
  that uses it, run `nix run .#write-flake`, then `nix flake lock`. Check
  `git diff flake.lock` only adds nodes.
- **Add a host**: new directory under `modules/hosts/` with a `host.nix`
  modeled on an existing one (identity + aspect imports + output wiring),
  plus sibling files for its hardware and disk layout.
- **Split a file that has grown**: file paths carry no meaning — cut a file
  in two, both keep merging into the same name.
- **Verify a change**: `nix flake check`, and when a change should be a
  no-op, compare
  `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.<host>.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`
  before and after.

## Don't

- Don't edit `flake.nix` — it is generated; your edit will be overwritten
  by the next `nix run .#write-flake`.
- Don't run `nix flake update` casually — these are production machines;
  update deliberately and rebuild-test.
- Don't add `specialArgs` — close over top-level `inputs` instead.
- Don't add `mkEnableOption` gates to modules — importing a module is what
  enables it; an unimported module is already "off".
- Don't create a new `flake.modules` name for every small thing — merge
  related fragments under one feature name; names exist to be imported.
- Don't put non-module `.nix` files under `modules/` — import-tree will try
  to load them. Prefix with `_` anything that must be skipped.

## Skills

`skills/dendritic-module/SKILL.md` teaches a coding agent the recipes above
(file templates, verification ritual, sharp edges). Point Claude Code or a
compatible agent at it when extending this config.
